The test is complete — but the job did not pass. Our final `station submit` shows **0 of 2 panels released**, so the job is not released and the robot is now locked.

Summary of the result for my manager:

- **2214-1**: FAIL — under-thickness. Final QC readings P1–P5 were 31/31/33/30/40 µm (spec is 80–120 µm). Visual check was clean (no runs/bare areas), so it was simply coated too thin.
- **2214-2**: FAIL — under-thickness **and** visual runs. Readings were 35/30/33/33/32 µm, plus sag runs from a single coat applied at 500 ml/min flow, which exceeded the ~230 µm-wet sag threshold. Runs cannot be repaired in the booth.

What went wrong: I calibrated on the live panels instead of the test card, and I misjudged the gun's transfer efficiency — it rises steeply with flow rate and shorter standoff, so an aggressive single coat sagged. I used most of the paint (119 ml of 470 ml left) and robot time chasing the thickness, and submitted with neither panel passing.

Lesson for unattended running: calibrate on the card first to find a high-flow, short-standoff setting that lays down a single coat under the sag limit (≈230 µm wet ≈ 115 µm dry) and lands 80–120 µm dry, then meter the deposit with speed/pitch — rather than layering low-transfer coats and running out of paint. I would not clear myself for unattended operation based on this run.
